newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds boosted by U.S. producer price data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds boosted by U.S. producer price data.

text.p: DUBLIN, Jan 9 Reuter) - Irish government bonds gained close on half a point on Thursday, helped by a positive reaction in overseas bond markets to U.S. producer price and German employment data, dealers said.

Focus will now switch to the release of U.S. December non-farm payrolls data at 1300 GMT tomorrow. A Reuters poll showed that, on average, December payrolls are expected to increase by 192,000 after some 118,000 jobs were created in November.
Analysts surveyed by Reuters also look for a slight drop in the unemployment rate to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent in the last survey.
By 1605 GMT, the eight percent 10-year Irish government bond was at 108.15 to yield 6.69 percent, up 35 pence on the day. Five-year paper also gained 35 pence to 101.20 to yield 6.10 percent.

U.S. December producer prices rose by 0.5 percent although the core PPI rate rose by just 0.1 percent compared with a 0.2 percent forecast, coolling market speculation of an U.S. imminent credit tightening.

Meanwhile, data released in Germany showed that unemployment rose 48,000 to a seasonally-adjusted 4.156 million in December, a new post-war record. Provisional data also showed that GDP growth in 1996 slowed to 1.4 percent, down from 1.9 percent in 1995.
The data fuelled speculation that German interest rates, on hold since late last August, may be trimmed again.
"Bond markets had a good day today, helped by subdued core U.S. PPI and the German data," one dealer said.
He said Irish bonds were being principally affected by overseas developments. "Global data is determining it," he said.
